symptom: The nightly agent dev-loop benchmark's apply-entity step read 108 units against a baseline of 107 (ako/mxcli#2555).
cause: The end-of-run 'Domain model X is not laid out' reminder (b38747a0b, via #1930) read the module unit with GetModule to skip Marketplace modules, every time it printed. The bench's session module is authored without @position, so the reminder fires on every entity edit there.
file: mdl/executor/exec_context.go (trackModifiedDomainModel takes the module and records its Marketplace flag), executor.go (layoutReminder reads the flag), 8 call sites
fix: The statement that changes a domain model already holds the module; trackModifiedDomainModel now takes it and notes whether it is a Marketplace module, and the reminder reads that instead of the unit.
insight: Bisect a counts-increased alert by commit range first (4 merges), then measure the step's own command with MXCLI_STATS_FILE on both builds: the plain alter entity on TestApp was equal (127/27 both), and equal counts redirected the search to what only fires on the bench's project shape — linked entities on the placement grid — where the difference reproduced as one unit-store hit (157 vs 156). A mock GetModule that fails the test turns the cost into an assertion.
test: mdl/executor/layout_reminder_test.go (the mock's GetModule now fails the test; the four reminder tests still pass, Marketplace skip included); reverting the read fails them; live: TestApp with a grid-placed module, alter entity: 157 unit-store hits on 2e845ff, 156 with the fix, reminder still printed
